previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with right-sided neck and head pain, transient vision loss, and ear drainage, following a recent diagnosis of classical Hodgkin lymphoma. Imaging revealed a rapidly enlarging nasopharyngeal mass with skull base and nerve involvement, explaining her symptoms. She received ICE chemotherapy and intrathecal methotrexate, with a lumbar puncture performed for CNS evaluation. During admission, she developed neutropenic fever, managed with cefepime, and mucositis, complicated by a methadone-fluconazole interaction, leading to a switch to micafungin. Her diabetes required insulin due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia, and she received a blood transfusion for symptomatic microcytic anemia. IVIG was administered for immunodeficiency. Her pain improved with optimized analgesia, including increased pregabalin. She stabilized, completed treatment, and was discharged home with follow-up in oncology, neuro-ophthalmology, and immunology.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MR ___ AND W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with history of nasopharyngeal lymphoma with
intracranial involvement, presents with lower back pain and left leg numbness.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal imaging was performed with T2, T1, and STIR technique.
Axial T2 imaging was performed.  After the administration of 5 mL intravenous
gadolinium axial and sagittal T1 imaging was performed.
FINDINGS: 

There are postoperative changes of L5 and S1 laminectomies with posterior
hardware stabilization including transpedicle screws and rods. Integrity of
hardware is not adequately evaluated by MRI technique. The vertebral body
heights throughout the lumbar spine are maintained.  There is no subluxation.
Areas of focal fat are seen within the L3 and L4 vertebral bodies. The bone
marrow signal of the lumbar spine is otherwise unremarkable without evidence
for focal malignancy.

The conus medullaris is normal in signal and morphology and a terminates at
the L1 level, as seen on sagittal imaging. There is no abnormal cord
parenchymal, leptomeningeal or epidural contrast enhancement.

At the L2-L3 level, there is mild bilateral facet arthropathy and a minimal
diffuse disc bulge.  The spinal canal and neural foramina are normal.

At the L3-L4 level, there is mild bilateral facet arthropathy and a minimal
diffuse disc bulge with mild bilateral neural foraminal narrowing.  The spinal
canal is normal.

At the L4-L5 level, there is bilateral facet arthropathy and a diffuse disc
bulge with left foraminal disc protrusion which causes mild spinal canal
narrowing and mild right neural foraminal narrowing and mild to moderate left
neural foraminal narrowing.

At the L5-S1 level, the spinal canal is decompressed posteriorly. There is
severe loss of disc height and signal, and a disc bulge with posterior
endplate osteophytes. There is bilateral facet arthropathy. In addition, there
is anterior epidural soft tissue which is T1 hyperintense, post-contrast T1
hyperintense, and T2 hyperintense. These signal characteristics are compatible
with either a small disc protrusion or postoperative granulation tissue,
though granulation tissue would be more commonly load signal on precontrast T1
weighted images. This finding is completely unchanged compared to ___ in ___. Overall, this causes mild spinal canal narrowing with
posterior displacement of the descending left S1 nerve root. There is also
probable moderate left and mild right neural foraminal narrowing although
evaluation is difficult secondary to metallic susceptibility artifact from
adjacent hardware.

The spleen is enlarged and measures up to 18.9 cm craniocaudad, image 1:14,
compared to 17.7 cm on the CT abdomen pelvis dated ___.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis ___.  MRI thoracic and lumbar spine
___.  Lumbar spine MRI ___.

IMPRESSION:


1. Postoperative change of L5-S1 laminectomies and posterior fusion. Anatomic
alignment. Unchanged anterior epidural abnormality at L5-S1, mildly narrowing
the spinal canal, with signal characteristics compatible with a small disc
protrusion or granulation tissue. There is unchanged posterior displacement of
the descending left S1 nerve root.
2. Unchanged lumbar spondylosis at other levels.
3. No evidence of leptomeningeal, epidural, or osseous malignancy.
4. Splenomegaly, slightly increased compared to CT abdomen/ pelvis dated ___.

EXAMINATION:  LUMBAR PUNCTURE (W/ FLUORO)

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with CVID, DLBCL, Hodgkin lymphoma  // request
LP and IT MTX administration, no L5-S1-disc pain, L4-L5 please

TECHNIQUE:  After informed consent was obtained from the patient explaining 
the risks, benefits, and alternatives to the procedure, the patient was laid 
in prone position on the fluoroscopic table. A preprocedure time-out was
performed confirming the patient's identity, relevant history, procedure to be
performed and labs.

Puncture was performed at L3-4, as there was previously difficulty with access
at L4-5 and L5-S1.  Approximately  5 cc of 1% lidocaine was administered for
local anesthesia. Under fluoroscopic guidance, a 20 gauge spinal needle was
inserted into the thecal sac. There was good return of clear CSF. 10 cc of CSF
were collected in 4 tubes and sent for requested analysis. 6 cc of
methotrexate was administered intrathecally by the oncologist. All instruments
were then withdrawn.

COMPARISON:  ___ lumbar puncture.

FINDINGS: 

Intact L5-S1 fusion hardware.

IMPRESSION: 

Successful lumbar puncture with administration of intrathecal methotrexate by
the oncologist. 10 cc of clear CSF were collected in 4 tubes and sent for
analysis.

I, Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the key components of
the above procedure and I reviewed and agree with the trainee's findings and
dictation.
